newsitem.title: USA: Heinz to announce revamp, sees EPS growth.
newsitem.headline: Heinz to announce revamp, sees EPS growth.

text.p: H.J. Heinz Co reported stronger third-quarter earnings and repeated it will announce restructuring plans later Friday it believes will generate earnings per share growth of 10-12 percent until 2000.

The company, whose brands include Heinz, StarKist, 9-Lives, Ore-Ida and Weight Watchers, had record third-quarter earnings per share of $0.48, excluding non-recurring items, up 14.3 percent from the year ago's $0.42. Including non- recurring items -- a charge of $0.03 for restructuring and related costs and a gain of $0.02 from the sale of some land in the U.K. -- earnings per share were $0.47, an 11.9 percent increase.
Net sales for the quarter increased 5.2 percent to $2.31 billion.

"The record third quarter results are excellent, but they are only a prelude to the reorganization that we will announce later today in San Francisco at 9:00 a.m. Pacific time, (1200 EST/1700 GMT) " said Heinz chairman and chief executive Anthony J. F. O'Reilly.

"In that reorganization presentation we will tell our shareholders the result of Project Millennia, as we call it, and of our plans for the future, which we believe will materially improve our business, improve shareholder value and generate solid earnings per share growth of 10-12 percent into the next millennium."
The company's core segments are ketchup and condiments, tuna, weight control, pet food, infant food and food service.
As previously reported, Heinz has been divesting businesses that do not fit the core units and is attempting to shed more.
